subject: Next: POC success metrics & timeline — proposed evaluation sprint for Hearthwell
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@hearthwell.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Demo follow-up + proposed 3-week eval sprint (success criteria, owners, next steps)

Hi Tom — thanks again for the demo call this morning. Appreciated the clear breakdown of Hearthwell's ingestion patterns and the two high-priority use cases (clinical note summarization + triage routing). Per our conversation, I’m proposing a short, focused evaluation sprint to validate latency, cost per 1k tokens, and throughput for your peak-concurrency window.

High-level proposed plan (3 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep, 2–3 days): connect dev creds, share small sample dataset (anonymized), and baseline run with a 5k-token traffic replay.
- Week 1 (integration + initial runs): run 50K tokens/day across representative prompts to measure median p95 latency and per-token cost on an adjusted Redwood-verified model profile.
- Week 2 (stress & regression): validate batching/kv-cache savings, measure 95th/99th percentile latency at 2x concurrent sessions, and run quality checks vs. your reference prompts.
- Week 3 (handoff & acceptance): produce short evaluation report, align on any quantization or routing changes, and sign off on success criteria.

Proposed success criteria (pass/fail):
1) p95 latency for 512-token prompts <= 300ms in your primary region (us-west).
2) End-to-end throughput to support 120 qps with median latency < 200ms under planned batching.
3) Per-token inference cost reduction >= 25% vs your current baseline (post-batching/quantization recommendations).
4) No material quality regressions on the 30-reference prompt set (benchmarked via perplexity + spot human checks).

Owners & points of contact:
- Redwood (Naomi): overall POC lead, scheduling, access requests.
- Redwood (Marcus): runtime tuning, model/quantization recommendations.
- Hearthwell (Tom): data owners for sample set, api keys, and acceptance sign-off.
- Hearthwell (Susan): clinical SME for quality sign-off.

Attachments: short checklist + evaluation matrix (attached). I included an editable spreadsheet with the 30-reference prompts and the proposed acceptance thresholds.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm sample dataset availability and target date for first replay (proposed Mon 11/23).
2) Accept the high-level success criteria or propose adjustments by EOD Mon 11/23.
3) I'll send a calendar hold for a 30-min kickoff once we agree on data access.

If that plan looks good, we’ll aim to have preliminary numbers by the end of week 1.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + proposed 3-week eval sprint (success criteria, owners, next steps)

Naomi — thanks for the clear write-up and the checklist. A few quick clarifications from our side before we lock timelines:

1) Data: we can provide a de-identified sample set (10K notes) by Tue 11/24, is that enough for the replay baseline?
2) Acceptance thresholds: the p95 target looks aggressive — is that measured on a cold start or with KV cache enabled? In production we'll be using short-lived KV cache for repeated patient histories.
3) Who needs access on our side? I can provide API keys to a service account; Susan will be primary for quality checks. We may also copy in engineering (Chris Park) if low-level network access is required.

If you can confirm the KV cache assumption and whether 10K notes suffices, we’ll aim for the Tue replay.

—Tom
Tom Reyes
Head of Product Engineering | Hearthwell Labs
Tom.Reyes@hearthwell.com | +1 (650) 555-1180

Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + proposed 3-week eval sprint (success criteria, owners, next steps)

Thanks Tom — quick answers below and a small tweak to the plan to reflect KV caching: 

1) Sample size: 10K de-identified notes is fine for the baseline replay; we’ll sample ~5k for the 512-token runs and keep the rest for longer-context and stress tests.
2) Latency measurement: p95 target assumes KV cache warmed for repeated prompts (we'll warm cache during the Week 1 runs). We’ll report both cold and warmed p95/p99 in the evaluation matrix.
3) Access: a service account with API key + network allowlist for Redwood’s IPs is sufficient. If Chris Park needs to be looped for networking, that’s fine — please CC him on the access ticket.

Small change: to allow time for network allowlisting, can we shift the kickoff replay to Wed 11/25 (morning)? That gives your infra team a day to open ports. If that works, Week 1 numbers would land by the following Wed.

I attached the editable matrix (hearthwell_eval_matrix.xlsx) and a short runbook in the PDF. I’ll send calendar invites once you confirm the 11/25 kickoff and list of users for access.

Best — Naomi

Adding a quick technical note from the runtime side — thanks for the plan Naomi. A couple of items I’ll own during the sprint:

- Pre-kickoff: I’ll share a small terraform snippet for allowlisting and a short network checklist to avoid surprises.
- Week 1: I’ll run an initial template with our quantized variant and a conservative batch config; we can iterate after we see the first baseline numbers.
